whatContradictedTheCard: The dispatch's premise that the column set must be freshly derived from a type named Tier1FacetPayload/Tier2EnvelopeFacet was wrong -- that name does not exist in hauska-engine. The real 65-rail column set (including permits and easements, which the dispatch asked to add 'now') was already built and merged by a prior PARCEL-RECORD card.

The dispatch's premise that 'unaccounted vs row-absence' was an open empirical question was largely already settled by a live CHECK constraint enforcing unaccounted as an explicit stored sentinel -- CP1 confirmed this by schema, not by inference, but it was not this card's discovery to make from scratch.

CP1's own cost estimate for the six-county plan ('cheap and safe, under 10 seconds') was based on aggregate GROUP BY queries and did not predict the real loader's cost -- 101.5 seconds to fully materialize the smallest county's cell rows. This is a genuine, unresolved scaling question for whoever builds the cross-repo caller, not a defect in this card's own read pattern.

The standing memory figure of '3,556 uniform cells' for the dead county-rail ledger conflates a theoretical denominator (254 counties x 14 rails) with an observed row count. The live county_facet_coverage table holds 1,817 rows and is not literally uniform on every field -- the stronger, corrected evidence for its dead disposition is that it has not been recomputed in 10 days while its replacement is written every few minutes.
